title: Containers
summary: Laravel owns intent: definitions, authorization, AI orchestration and the public API. Go executes activated definitions in the data plane. Desired state lives in Laravel, applied state is reported by Go, and both fence work by generation.

boxes.label: Portal
boxes.detail: Devices, profiles, dashboards, automations, alerts, integrations and settings. It polls the API; there is no realtime push.

boxes.label: Admin
boxes.detail: Organizations, users, roles, permission ceilings and retention.

boxes.label: broker-admin
boxes.detail: Applies credentials and ACLs to Mosquitto Dynamic Security, so each organization's credentials are confined to its own Sparkplug group.

boxes.label: API
boxes.detail: Public, integration and internal APIs. Code is organized by domain, each with its own routes, models and services.

boxes.label: Workers
boxes.detail: Automation, alerts, webhooks, assistant and device-adapter workers, plus the scheduler. Same codebase as the API.

boxes.label: adapter-manager
boxes.detail: Starts and updates one adapter runtime per tenant.

boxes.label: MQTT broker
boxes.detail: The platform broker. Tenant identity comes from the authenticated connection, never from the payload.

boxes.label: PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB
boxes.detail: One database, two owners. Laravel owns the public schema. Go owns device_runtime: telemetry, latest state, outboxes, rule and DAG state.

boxes.label: Tenant adapter runtime
boxes.detail: Per tenant: a Mosquitto ingress broker and a Node-RED runtime that runs the decoder and republishes Sparkplug B.

boxes.label: NATS JetStream
boxes.detail: Durable streams inside the data plane: control, runtime events, telemetry before storage and committed telemetry. Laravel has no NATS client.

steps.text: A device publishes Sparkplug B to the platform broker. Its credentials confine it to its organization's group.
The runtime is the Sparkplug host application. It subscribes per broker connection and never asks Laravel how to process a message.
Readings take a durable hop through JetStream before storage, so telemetry keeps flowing while Laravel or the database is briefly down.
The runtime writes observations, latest values and diagnostics to its own schema.
The portal asks the API for latest values and history.
The API authorizes the request, then reads from the runtime over internal HTTP. It also pushes definitions this way.
The runtime claims Laravel's outbox rows and posts back what it applied, so desired and applied state stay separate.
Vendor devices join the same path: the tenant's adapter runtime republishes their data as Sparkplug B.
Open the runtime to follow one reading through it.
